```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 1](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop1.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the `command_line` folder:

```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
pwd
```

Replace the text below each heading with your own notes. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk like the one above.

## Basic unix commands

Notes on `pwd`, `ls`, `cd` and how unix commands are put together.

Notes on `cat`, `head`, `grep` and `man`.
